Using `edgeFraction` allows for faster convergence at the cost of potential sub-optimality [S3, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the notes for `options.edgeFraction`: 'Fraction of total edges to sample for potential collapses, used to improve performance by avoiding full mesh scan.' This supports the 'faster convergence' (improved performance) part of the claim. The claim also mentions 'potential sub-optimality'. While the evidence does not explicitly use the word 'sub-optimality', it describes a stochastic sampling process (`FindValidCollapses` generates random indices) and a heuristic-based selection (penalizing high-degree vertices, using QEF error thresholds). In algorithmic contexts, sampling a subset of candidates rather than evaluating all possibilities inherently carries the risk of missing the globally optimal collapse, which is the definition of potential sub-optimality. Since the evidence supports the mechanism (sampling for speed) and the nature of the mechanism (heuristic/stochastic sampling) implies the trade-off mentioned, the claim is supported by the provided text.
